feedback: The geometry changes helped by moving the rear sensors further back (y from -0.01 to -0.02) and increasing the wheel track from 0.16 to 0.17, which should enable earlier detection of sharp turns and improve lateral stability. However, the race data shows the robot still fails to complete the tracks with one line loss event per run and off-track termination around 60% progress, indicating the controller has not fully exploited these geometry improvements yet. The controller had to compensate for the still challenging line loss events and off-track failures, suggesting the need for stronger and more responsive control parameters. Requested changes: 1) Increase wheel_track further to 0.18 to enhance stability during turns. 2) Move rear sensors even further back to y = -0.03 to detect turns earlier. 3) Consider slightly increasing sensor_size to 0.016 (already at max) or adjusting sensor x-positions to better cover the rear area for earlier line detection. These changes aim to provide the controller with better early line information and a more stable platform, reducing line loss events and improving completion and progress.
